steps: Anonymous /studio-lab; add Middle East at 0 (music clip) or import a video clip; for the brace variant create loop 2-4
Dispatch pointerdown (pointerId 1, touch) on the clip header (or on the loop brace), then pointerdown (pointerId 2) on the same element, as with two fingers or pen + mouse
pointerup id 2, pointerup id 1 (also window pointerup/pointercancel id 1)
Real Ctrl+Z, click the Undo button, real Delete
bugs.expected: After both pointers are released, the gesture count returns to 0 and Undo/Redo and edits work (D-20: a gesture clears its own state)
bugs.actual: Permanently blocked. The status shows 'Undo/Redo drag-ის დროს არ მუშაობს — ჯერ ხელი აუშვი.' or 'რედაქტირება drag-ის დროს არ მუშაობს…', and history is unchanged. Only a reload recovers, which loses the demo arrangement. Read-only cause: ArrangementClip beginGesture overwrites gestureRef.current without calling the previous gesture's release(), and the watchUncapturedPointerGesture handler returns early because gestureRef.current !== gesture, so gestureCountRef stays at 1 or more. Scope confirmed in the browser: ArrangementClip (music and video clips) and ArrangementLoopBrace leak; ArrangementRuler (releases previous dragRef first) and the lane marquee (calls marqueeCleanupRef first) recover, Ctrl+Z works. The root cause does not depend on the capture path. With successful capture (a real two-finger touch), pointerdown 2 overwrites g1 without releasing it, pointerup 2 releases g2 and nulls gestureRef, and pointerup 1 returns early, so the count stays at 1. The early return in the uncaptured listener is a secondary symptom. ArrangementContext.test.ts lines 200-201 already pass for nested beginPointerGesture, so the fix and its test belong in ArrangementClip and ArrangementLoopBrace; the ruler's dragRef.current?.release() before overwriting is the in-repo pattern.
